The *Jātipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 460) is a verse text preserved in the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the biographical and karmic narrative associated with the elder (thera) Jātipupphiya. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No independent parallels are identified in SuttaCentral, but automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive formulaic text reuse within Pali canonical and commentarial literature, recording 122 matching passages across 49 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest relationship appears with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), where segments 0.3–6.4 correspond closely to the commentarial biography (§46_7–58) [DharmaNexus]. The concluding verses of the text (segments 6.1–11.1) consist largely of stock apadāna formulas, exhibiting extensive textual overlap with neighboring texts in the *Therāpadāna* and *Therīapadāna*, including the *Paṭṭipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 461), *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430), *Tiṇukkadhāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 456), and *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 459) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects minor cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* [DharmaNexus].
